scenes.scene: A South African woman farmer kneels on a PATH beside a small vegetable bed, gently spreading dry leaf mulch over exposed soil with her hands. Healthy young plants, crumbly soil, mulch kept clear of stems, corrugated-roof homestead and green KwaZulu-Natal hills in the distance. Teaching focus: care for living soil.

At a modest South African homestead outdoor table, a farming family shares a simple meal with fresh vegetables from their nearby garden. The mother places a bowl of leafy vegetables on the table; eggs and a small harvest basket nearby. Respectful everyday realism, healthy ordinary family, no poverty spectacle. Teaching focus: keep farm food for the household.

Two neighbouring Black South African women farmers exchange a small basket of harvested maize and plain seed envelopes across a low garden gate. An open compost bay with plant scraps in the background, modest homesteads and gardens. Friendly unposed interaction; no writing on packets. Teaching focus: share surplus and return resources.

A South African woman and man farmer stand safely on a firm path after a gentle rain, observing small surface runoff routes across their sloping homestead garden. One points at shallow water following the slope while the other holds a notebook. Wet earth and overcast clearing light. No digging, no hazardous flood, no glowing arrows.

A clear slightly elevated view from a modest South African kitchen doorway to herbs and small vegetable beds immediately beside the house, water container nearby, paths connecting them; further away are larger beds and fruit trees. One woman harvests leafy greens close to the door. Teaching focus: frequently used plants close to home. No rings, diagrams or labels.

Two Black South African farmers sit at a rustic outdoor table discussing a simple hand-drawn site sketch, looking between paper and their actual smallholding beyond. Sketch shows house, paths, beds and trees in the same general arrangement visible behind. Pencil and blank notebook, no legible writing, compass numbers or invented measurements. Eye-level over-shoulder view.

A Black South African man and woman carefully use a simple wooden A-frame contour level on a gentle grassy slope. Both feet sit on the ground; the woman holds the top steadily and the man points to the centre of the crossbar. A few marker pegs trace a nearly horizontal line across the slope. No text or measurements.

A South African smallholder observes the long coherent shadow of a corrugated-roof house extending across a proposed garden patch on a crisp winter morning. Low sunlight from upper left; every shadow falls to lower right. Farmer holds notebook on the sunny path and considers where beds would receive light. No snow or falling leaves blanket. Cool dry grass, warm sun.

Close environmental portrait of a Black South African woman farmer squatting beside a small spade-cut soil opening at the edge of her garden, comparing a crumb of soil in her palm with roots and naturally occurring grass nearby. No exaggerated indicator species or labels. Good hand anatomy, dark topsoil visible, practical observation, green hills background.

Two South African smallholder learners walk a safe hillside path with a clipboard, studying their homestead's land: upper slope, lower garden, tree shade and a small drainage hollow all legible in a wide environmental composition.
